summary: Defines the format and usage of the DetNet service Associated Channel on DetNet networks with an MPLS data plane. This channel can carry test packets of active Operations, Administration, and Maintenance (OAM) protocols, used to detect failures and measure performance.

eli5.summary: Some networks promise packets arrive on time. This sets up a special side lane for sending test packets to check that the promise holds and to spot breakages.

questions: how does detnet oam work with mpls
subtitle: Defines the DetNet Associated Channel Header that lets test packets of OAM protocols ride alongside DetNet flows over MPLS.

tldr.problem: Deterministic Networking over an MPLS data plane needs a way to detect failures and measure performance, and its per-packet replication and elimination functions need extra fields that ordinary pseudowire OAM does not carry.
tldr.mechanism: A DetNet Associated Channel Header (d-ACH) follows the S-Label and carries a version, an 8-bit sequence number, a channel type, the originating node ID, a level and a session ID, so active OAM test packets share the flow's path.
tldr.outcome: Active OAM protocols such as BFD can monitor DetNet flows end to end, including across TSN and DetNet IP segments.

today: RFC 9546 is a Proposed Standard from February 2024 and has not been obsoleted or updated. It builds on the DetNet MPLS data plane of RFC 8964.

sections.title: Why DetNet Needs Its Own OAM
sections.content:
RFC 8655 describes the Deterministic Networking (DetNet) architecture, including Packet Replication, Elimination, and Ordering Functions (PREOF) that keep packet loss low. OAM (Operations, Administration, and Maintenance) protocols detect and localize defects and monitor performance. Some functions, such as failure detection, run proactively; others, such as defect localization, run on demand.

This document presents a format for active OAM in DetNet networks with the MPLS data plane, and defines the usage of the DetNet service Associated Channel, building on RFC 8964.
sections.eli5: A delivery service that promises on-time arrival also needs inspectors. This RFC gives the inspectors a way to send test parcels along the same road.

sections.title: How Active OAM Is Encapsulated
sections.content:
In an MPLS underlay, DetNet flows are encapsulated like pseudowires. DetNet OAM reuses the pseudowire Associated Channel Header idea from RFC 4385, but a DetNet pseudowire acts like a multi-segment pseudowire whose service sub-layer functions work per packet, not per segment. PREOF therefore needs extra fields for proper OAM packet handling.

An OAM packet is stacked as: the DetNet OAM payload, the d-ACH, the S-Label (the service label that identifies the flow), optional F-Labels (forwarding labels), then data-link and physical layers. When MPLS runs over UDP/IP per RFC 9025, a UDP and IP header sit beneath the labels. A DetNet flow is identified by the S-Label, which MUST be at the bottom of the stack, and an active OAM packet MUST include the d-ACH immediately after it.
sections.eli5: The test packet is wrapped in layers like a parcel: a test label, the flow's service tag, then the road labels. The special tag always sits right after the service tag.

sections.title: The d-ACH Format
sections.content:
The header is two 32-bit words. Its fields are:

  • First nibble: MUST be 0b0001, so the packet is told apart from an IP packet and from a DetNet data packet.
  • Version: 4 bits; this document specifies version 0.
  • Sequence Number: an unsigned circular 8-bit field. The originator MUST set it, the initial value SHOULD be random, and it SHOULD increase by 1 for each active OAM packet. Other strategies are allowed, for example negative testing of ordering functions.
  • Channel Type: 16 bits, MUST be a value from the IANA G-ACh Types registry.
  • Node ID: an unsigned 20-bit field naming the originating DetNet node. It MUST be unique in the DetNet domain; how it is distributed is out of scope.
  • Level: 3 bits, analogous to the Maintenance Domain Level in IEEE 802.1Q, used to cope with the all-active-path forwarding of PREOF and to build hierarchies of OAM domains.
  • Flags: 5 one-bit flags, all unused. They MUST be 0 on transmission and ignored on receipt.
  • Session ID: 4 bits, distinguishing simultaneous OAM sessions from the same node at the same level.
sections.eli5: The special tag holds a name for the sender, a counter, a test type and a session number, so the receiver knows exactly which test it is looking at.

sections.title: Interaction with PREOF
sections.content:
PREOF can be applied to a DetNet flow at the service sub-layer to reduce loss and keep packets in order. For an active OAM packet, PREOF MUST use the d-ACH Sequence Number as its sequencing information. App-flow packets and OAM packets use different sequence number spaces.

The Sequence Number runs from 0 through 255. The RFC says that is enough, because active OAM packets are sent far less often than packets of an application flow, so wrapping around is not an issue. The Elimination sub-function always uses the S-Label together with the sequence number, while Replication uses the S-Label only.
sections.eli5: Test packets get their own counter, separate from the real traffic, and since there are few of them a small counter is enough.

sections.title: Interworking with TSN and DetNet IP
sections.content:
OAM domains of different technologies can interwork in a peering model, where state changes are mapped between domains or reported to a controller, or in a tunneling model, where one OAM protocol's test packets travel with the data flow, so test and data packets share fate.

For TSN, the peering model with Connectivity Fault Management requires the border node to support RFC 7023. BFD (RFC 5880, RFC 5885) can be used in the DetNet MPLS domain, and performance monitoring can use RFC 6374 in DetNet MPLS and Y.1731 in TSN. In the tunneling model, active OAM test packets MUST map to the same TSN Stream ID as the monitored flow and MUST be processed in the TSN domain by S-Label and Traffic Class. The remote endpoint must support the chosen OAM protocol.

For DetNet IP, using the same protocol such as BFD on both segments simplifies mapping errors, and STAMP (RFC 8762 and RFC 8972) can measure packet loss and delay.
sections.eli5: When a parcel crosses from one delivery company to another, the inspectors either pass notes between companies or send the test parcel along with the real one.

sections.title: IANA Registry for d-ACH Flags
sections.content: IANA created the DetNet Associated Channel Header (d-ACH) Flags registry. The registration procedure is IETF Review. It covers the five flag bits in the Flags field, and bits 0 to 4 are all currently unassigned.
sections.eli5: There are five blank switches reserved for later. Anyone who wants to use one has to ask permission.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The security considerations of the DetNet specifications, RFC 8655, RFC 8964 and RFC 9055, and of the OAM framework draft apply here. Security concerns related to MPLS OAM tools such as LSP Ping (RFC 8029) and BFD over pseudowires (RFC 5885) also apply. The RFC adds no new security mechanism of its own.
sections.eli5: The same safety rules as the rest of the delivery system apply to the inspectors too.

fields.name: Sequence Number
fields.desc: Circular counter set by the originator.

fields.name: Channel Type
fields.desc: A value from the IANA G-ACh Types registry.

fields.name: Flags
fields.desc: Five unused flags; MUST be 0 on transmission.

fields.name: Session
fields.desc: Distinguishes OAM sessions from one node.
